sections.text: Thirty-three trials of BTK inhibitors are recorded in multiple sclerosis (MS), with 18 in Phase 3, 11 in Phase 2, and 4 in Phase 1.
Sponsors include Sanofi (10 trials), Roche and Merck KGaA (5 each), Novartis (4), and smaller contributions from Zenas BioPharma, Guangzhou Lupeng, and others.
Six trials have stopped, including five evobrutinib trials (Merck KGaA) terminated due to lack of efficacy or changes in trial design.
Evobrutinib failed to meet its primary endpoint of annualized relapse rate in two Phase 3 trials (NCT04338022, NCT04338061) and one Phase 2 trial (NCT02975349), all terminated.
Evobrutinib’s maximum phase in MS is 3, with no approvals, and its development in relapsing MS was stopped due to lack of efficacy versus teriflunomide.
Pirtobrutinib (Loxo Oncology) was withdrawn from a Phase 2 MS trial (NCT06104683) for sponsor decision, with no plans to continue.
A 2026 review notes that BTK inhibitors target both adaptive and innate immunity, with modulation of myeloid cell and microglial activation relevant to MS pathology.
Recent literature (2026) indicates BTK inhibitors show promising effects on inflammatory activity in MS, with emerging signals on disability progression.
A 2026 review highlights that fenebrutinib, tolebrutinib, and other BTK inhibitors are in late development for MS with potential to target both relapsing and progressive forms via CNS penetration.
The site’s risk model estimates a median 24% stop risk across ongoing BTK inhibitor trials in MS, with 8 trials analyzed.
BTK inhibitors are positioned as oral agents with potential CNS penetration to modulate microglia, differing from anti-CD20 biologics that primarily target peripheral B cells.

read: Mechanism evidence: BTK inhibition targets both B cells and CNS-resident microglia, with preclinical and clinical signals in MS inflammation and progression.
Competitive position: Despite evobrutinib's failure, the mechanism remains active with multiple Phase 3 programs; median stop risk is 24%.
Open questions: Will any BTK inhibitor demonstrate superiority over current therapies in relapsing or progressive MS, and can safety risks like liver toxicity or infection be managed long-term?
would_change: A Phase 3 success from tolebrutinib or remibrutinib would strengthen support.
A safety signal or new termination in an ongoing Phase 3 trial would increase risk.
